**What I changed:**
1. **ASTM split into two lanes.** The old batch script reads its list of designs one line at a time. It had just read p077 (design 16 of 43). I cut the list file at that point (full copy kept in `astm_list.full.txt`), so the script finishes p077 and then stops by itself.
   - Lane R started at 10:10 and is working from the end of the list (p146).
   - Lane F starts when the old batch prints "ASTM BATCH DONE". Both lanes are covered by `resume_all.sh` if the server restarts.
2. **Fixed my own mistake.** My first lane F waiter would never have started, because its check matched its own command line. I deleted that session of mine and recreated it to wait for the "ASTM BATCH DONE" line instead.
3. **Re-pinned two p146 tests** (shear45 and torsion) to cores within one NUMA node; their core sets had spanned two nodes.

**Watch next hour:**
- When lane F starts, ASTM and push-out together will ask for 36 cores on a 32-core quota, so expect some throttling. If it goes above 30%, I'll lower the cores per test in `ops/astm_lanes.sh`.
- The pinning service may again give new tests core sets that span two NUMA nodes; those will need re-pinning.
- p077 is slow, like p076 was: time steps are around 1e-4.
